leak.verdict: No leak found. I checked four ways and found no route by which Blocksworld-hard instances, reference plans or results could have shaped Pa_v3's training data or H2's settings. (1) None of the 240 distillation problems is isomorphic to any of the 110 hard instances. No pair even shares the coarse invariant. No training row in mix_v3, mix_v2c, distill_rows or the full v2 set restates a hard (init, goal) problem. (2) Distillation goals do overlap with hard goal configurations, but only at the rate seen for generated sets: mirror and b3fresh overlap just as much. H2's gain falls mostly on instances with no shared goal and on 11-15 blocks, outside the 6-10-block distillation range. (3) Of the four scripts, only the exclusion code in bw_distill.problems() and bw_b3_prep.fresh() reads the hard PDDL files. No script reads hard plans (info.json) or any hard result. (4) H2's arguments equal FREEZE_B2_beam exactly except `pa`. The B2 beam settings were chosen on val_large and val_v2 only, before any hard run. The H2 freeze was written before H1 ran, and no shard was rerun because of its results. The only effect hard had on the data was through exclusion, which moved the training set away from hard: 10 candidate problems were rejected by the coarse hard invariant, and none of them was a true isomorph. Remaining caveats concern scope and provenance, not leaks.
findings: (1) ISOMORPHISM, 0 FOUND. I wrote an exact canonical form for renaming: each block has four labelled ports (state-below, state-above, goal-below, goal-above) plus unary and nullary facts, and the code is the minimum over roots of a port-ordered BFS, per connected component. Against the repo's brute-force B.signature it agreed on 3,100 random problems (n 3-6, including hand-holding states and partial goals): 655 classes, 0 disagreements in either direction. It is also invariant under renaming for 2,000 problems at n 6-15 and for all 110 hard instances × 20 renamings, which give 110 distinct classes. Results: 0/240 distillation problems are isomorphic to a hard instance, and 0 distill-hard pairs share even VL.invariant. I also replayed bw_distill.problems(240) from the current code: all 240 (objs, init, goal) match solutions.jsonl exactly. No row's (state, goal) is isomorphic to any hard (init, goal) in mix_v3 (8,508 rows), mix_v2c (8,508), distill_rows (4,254) or all of BW_data_v2/proposer_actions_train.jsonl (53,682, Pa_v2's training data).

(1b) HOW HARD AFFECTED THE DISTILL SET: through exclusion only. Replaying the RNG stream, the generator rejected 10 candidates because they matched a hard invariant, 33 for val_large/mirror invariants, and 2 None draws. None of the 10 hard-invariant rejections was an exact isomorph; for example, slot 23 was rejected on the invariant (10, (1,1,2,3,3), (10,)) shared with instance-58. So hard influenced which problems were drawn only by pushing near-misses out. This is the opposite of a leak.

(2) GOAL-CONFIGURATION OVERLAP is common, but no higher than chance. Counting goal configuration up to renaming including the block count: 136/240 distillation problems share a goal configuration with some hard instance, and 31/110 hard instances have theirs among the distillation goals. Those 31 are 31 of the 36 hard instances with n<=10; the 5 without a match are instance-101, 37, 56, 72 and 81. Row counts: distill_rows 2,480/4,254, mix_v3 2,889/8,508, mix_v2c 832/8,508 (all of them instance-1's 6-block single tower), all v2 rows 5,232/53,682 (also only instance-1). Ignoring blocks the goal does not mention, 38/110 hard instances match, 4 of them with n 11-12 (instance-17, 29, 70, 12). Chance baseline for n<=10: mirror 33/36, b3fresh 31/36, hard 31/36.

(2b) STATE-AND-GOAL COINCIDENCES WITH HARD TRAJECTORIES are also at chance. 831 distill rows match, up to renaming, a (state, goal) pair on some hard trajectory. Most are near the goal: of the 679 rows matching B2-beam trajectories, 556 have <= 8 actions remaining, and 25 is the maximum. The same count against mirror's B2-beam trajectories is 649 rows over 28 instances, vs hard's 679 over 29. For v3-direct trajectories: hard 446/14, mirror 314/18, b3fresh 208/14.

(2c) H2's gain does not come from goal overlap. H2 discordant pairs (v3_only/b2_only): instances whose goal is not among the distillation goals 17/4; instances whose goal is 3/1. By size: 11-15 blocks (outside the distillation range) 17/4; 6-10 blocks 3/1. For H1, the gain is in range: 8 of its 10 v3_only wins are on instances whose goal is among the distillation goals, and 9 of 10 are at 6-10 blocks. That matches the in-range effect on b3fresh, where goal overlap is equally common.

(3) STATIC READS. bw_distill.py:36-38 reads bench/planbench/blocksworld_hard/generated/*.pddl (parse_problem, hard_signatures, invariants) for exclusion only. It also reads val_large/mirror, FREEZE_B2_beam.json args and its own output files. It never reads info.json (hard reference plans) or anything under BW_TEST_B2 or BW_B3_HARD. bw_b3_prep.py: fresh() reads the hard PDDLs for exclusion and the block-count mix of the b3fresh test set, not training data. mix() reads only distill_rows.jsonl and V2_ROWS = runs/BW_data_v2/proposer_actions_train.jsonl (line 28). train_generic.py reads only --rows (line 43) and --init-adapter; lm.train_sft has no evaluation step and no other file reads. bw_b3_eval.py reads FREEZE_B3, the adapters, SETS = b3fresh and mirror (line 25), and the files it hashes. No hard file. bwmn/blocks_planner.py reads only its F cache. The distillation F cache's 15,030 keys are all 6-10 blocks, and every one has the block set of a distillation problem, so no cache from a hard run was merged in.

(3b) DATA PROVENANCE REBUILT. distill_rows.jsonl equals rows(solutions.jsonl) exactly. mix_v3 and mix_v2c equal distill_rows plus a random.Random(0).sample of v2 rows, exactly. F-predicted states equal the exact trajectories (0 differ). Pa_v3's metrics show rows=runs/BW_DISTILL_r1/mix_v3.jsonl (8,508), init_adapter Pa_v2 sha ee1c5aec, 400 steps, seed 1. The adapter sha 48c9d279 matches FREEZE_B3. Pa_v3 is the only distillation run and adapter; no BW_DISTILL_r0 or alternative mix, step count or adapter exists in runs/, _superseded or _failed.

(4) H2 SETTINGS were not tuned on hard. FREEZE_B3_H2 args differ from FREEZE_B2_beam only in pa (Pa_v2_s1 -> Pa_v3_s1). They come from bw_b3_hard.py:55 `args = dict(b2["args"], pa=PA_V3)`, and the script's sha 321ecd3e matches D-66. FREEZE_B2_beam was chosen by bw_freeze.py from BW_SELECT_v1/select.jsonl: 10 rows, sets {val_large: 5, val_v2: 5}, file mtime 10-08 13:55:00, before the first hard run (hard_direct 10-08 15:42). The gate wrote FREEZE_B3_H2.json at 10-10 20:29:17 from B3_REPORT (b3fresh), before H1 ran (10-11 01:45-01:54). All 8 H2 shard summaries match the freeze args with 0 mismatches. Each H2 shard holds the same instance ids in the same order as the B2 hard_beam shard.

(4b) SHARD RESTARTS were caused by the turn cap, not by results. BW_B3_HARD.stdout shows 'run H2 shard 2/8' and '6/8' twice each. bundleE.stdout logs 'b3-hard-run stopped at the 16200 s cap' at 04:18:23 and 08:57:37. The aborted attempts got only to rounds 1-2 and round 1 in progress.txt. blocks_eval writes plans and summary only at the end, so no results from those attempts existed. The restarted rounds 1-2 show 'F queries 0', meaning a cache-hit replay of the same F keys.

CAVEATS (not leaks): (a) Design-level knowledge of hard. The distillation generator imitates hard's published structure: whole-configuration tall-tower goals at 6-10 of hard's 6-15 blocks. B3 was designed after B2's hard results were known (bw_distill.py mtime 10-09 12:04 vs B2 hard_beam summary 10-09 06:17), and PREREG_B3 says so openly. So B2's allowed wording 'Trained only on <= 6-block problems' must not be applied to H1/H2. (b) FREEZE_B3 hashes MIX_META but not mix_v3.jsonl, and train_generic records no hash of the rows file. My exact rebuild and the mtimes (mix 16:52:35 < Pa_v3 18:17:47) close this gap. (c) B2 hard_beam ran on blocks_planner.py before D-53 (summary 06:17:45 < planner mtime 07:03:49), while H2 ran on 18a5f22b. D-53 states the default behaviour is unchanged. This is a comparability caveat, not a leak. (d) Components shared by both arms cannot explain the H2-B2 difference. F's training data is goal-blind, 4-6 blocks, v1. Pa_v2's data is 4-6 blocks with hard-signature and suffix exclusion; 0 rows are hard isomorphs, but 2,445 v2 rows are near-goal matches with instance-1. Possible pretraining contamination of the base model can't be checked from the repo.

claims.verdict:
The H1 and H2 numbers reproduce exactly from the VAL field. H2: Pa_v3 S-beam solved 88/110 (CP 95% CI 0.7130-0.8702) against 73/110 for frozen B2 S-beam. Discordant pairs were +20/-5, exact McNemar p = 0.004077. H1: Pa_v3 S-direct solved 13/110 (CI 0.0645-0.1936) against 5/110, discordant +10/-2, p = 0.038574. Both runs used the frozen B2 args with only `pa` changed, and the freeze hash chain is intact. I independently confirmed label precision of 1.0: all 211 F-verified plans are valid, and all 4,254 F-predicted row states are exact. I also confirmed that none of the 240 distillation problems is a renaming of any of the 110 hard instances.

Unpaired Fisher tests against the published zero-shot numbers favour H2 by a wide margin. Against DeepSeek-R1 (59/110) two-sided p = 5.2e-5, and against o1-preview (26/110) p = 2.5e-17.

The audit found one substantive over-claim. The 'o1-mini 10%' row is NOT zero-shot: it is o1-mini plus a sound-verifier loop (LRM-Modulo). o1-mini's direct score is 0.90% (1/110). This was confirmed from arXiv 2410.02162 Table 5 and by re-scoring the upstream per-instance file. The row is labelled zero-shot in four places: the PREREG_PLANBENCH B2 table, SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md, DECISIONS P-08 and the release README. Every comparison against it breaks B2's own rule against comparing to verifier-in-loop numbers.

Other problems:
- **P-13's reading over-generalizes.** 12 of the 13 H1 successes fall inside the 6-10-block distillation range, and the claim that the token cap limits the gain is stated as a cause without evidence.
- **P-13 is out of date.** It still says H2 'continues'.
- **The GitHub-export README adds 'only'** ('Trained only on plans its own world model verified'), which is false.
- **The B2 premise that published results are 'aggregate only' is wrong.** The upstream repo at the vendored commit has per-instance hard-set results.
- **B2's headline template cannot be reused for H2.** Its phrase 'Trained only on <= 6-block problems' is false for Pa_v3.
findings:
RECOMPUTED H2 (from runs/BW_B3_HARD/h2_beam/plans.jsonl vs runs/BW_TEST_B2/hard_beam/plans.jsonl, VAL field):
- Counts: 88/110 = 0.800 (CP 95% CI 0.7130-0.8702) vs 73/110 = 0.664 (CI 0.5673-0.7509). Same 110 IDs, no duplicates, val == success on every row.
- Paired: v3-only 20, B2-only 5, both 68. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.0040773 (mid-p 0.0025, one-sided 0.0020). This matches B3_HARD_REPORT.json.
- Verification: 88/88 F-verified plans are VAL-valid, and all 22 failures were unverified (budget 17, dead_end 5).
- Strata (post hoc): 6-10 blocks 34/36 vs 32/36 (+3/-1, p = 0.63); 11-15 blocks 54/74 vs 41/74 (+17/-4, p = 0.0072). The H2 gain is mostly OUTSIDE the 6-10-block distillation range.
- Compute is about the same: 8.2k vs 8.0k proposer tokens and 198 vs 187 unique F queries per instance.
- The Pa_v3 beam itself beats Pa_v3 direct: +75/-0, p = 5.3e-23.

RECOMPUTED H1 (h1_direct vs BW_TEST_B2/hard_direct):
- Counts: 13/110 = 0.118 (CI 0.0645-0.1936) vs 5/110 (CI 0.0149-0.1029).
- Paired: +10/-2, both 3. Exact McNemar p = 0.0385742, which matches the report.
- Multiplicity: Holm over the two registered hard contrasts gives H2 0.0082 and H1 0.039, so both survive. H1 would not survive Bonferroni (0.077).
- Gain is in range: 12 of the 13 successes are 6-10 blocks (6-10: +9/-2, p = 0.065; 11-15: 1/74 vs 0/74).
- Truncation: 24/110 Pa_v3 outputs hit gen_tokens = 256 and are exactly the 24 'unparseable' fails, all at 10 blocks or more. The B2 Pa_v2 direct run had 0 cap hits (max 214 tokens).
- Greedy decoding means a larger M could only turn truncated failures into possible successes. So 13/110 is a lower bound under the frozen cap, but the 24 truncated plans are unscored.

UNPAIRED FISHER (two-sided; n = 110 each; published counts R1 59, o1-preview 26, o1-mini 11 for the mislabelled 10%, o1-mini 1 for the true direct 0.9%):
- **H2, 88/110:** vs R1 +26.4 pp, p = 5.2e-5 (one-sided 2.6e-5). The result holds for any R1 count from 58 to 61 (p <= 1.6e-4). vs o1-preview p = 2.5e-17; vs o1-mini 10% p = 2.2e-27 (not a valid comparison); vs o1-mini direct 1/110 p = 1.0e-38.
- **B2 S-beam, 73/110:** vs R1 p = 0.0733 (one-sided 0.037); vs o1-preview p = 2.4e-10; vs o1-mini 10% p = 1.2e-18. These reproduce P-08.
- **H1, 13/110:** BELOW R1 (p = 3.0e-11) and BELOW o1-preview (p = 0.033). vs o1-mini 10% p = 0.83; vs o1-mini direct 1/110 p = 0.0013. The proposer alone must not be framed as competitive with the zero-shot LRMs.

PUBLISHED-NUMBER PROVENANCE:
- **R1 53.6% and o1-preview 23.6% hold up.** The LLMs-Planning README leaderboard (zero-shot; column 'Blocksworld Hard - PDDL - 110 instances') reads R1 53.6%, o1-preview 23.65%, o1-mini 10%. arXiv 2410.02162 v1 (the only arXiv version) Table 5 gives o1-preview Direct 23.65% / LRM-Modulo 98.2%, and o1-mini Direct 0.90% / LRM-Modulo 10%.
- **My re-score of the upstream per-instance files** (results_backprompting/blocksworld_hard at commit fc638a1a, the vendored commit), using my own exact simulator matched to the local instance-N.pddl files:
  - R1 step-0 (direct) 59/110 = 53.64%; the loop was never run.
  - o1-preview step-0 26/110 = 23.64%; loop 108/110 = 98.18%.
  - o1-mini step-0 1/110 = 0.91%; loop 11/110 = 10.00%.
  - The re-score agrees with the files' own verifier flags on every flagged instance (110/110, 84/84 plus 26 loop-terminated, 110/110). The prompts are zero-shot PDDL (one [PLAN] marker, no example).
- **Conclusion:** R1 59/110 and o1-preview 26/110 are genuine direct zero-shot numbers. o1-mini 10% is a verifier-in-loop number.
- **The 'TMLR 2025' attribution for R1's hard-set number is unverified.** The fact-check could not open the TMLR PDF, and arXiv 2410.02162 v1 has no R1. Cite the leaderboard or per-instance file instead.
- The papers describe the set as '6 to 20 blocks', but the actual instances have 6-15 blocks, as our documents correctly state.

OVER-CLAIM 1 (HIGH), o1-mini 10% labelled zero-shot. It appears in four places:
- PREREG_PLANBENCH.md line 111, a table headed 'zero-shot generalists' with the row '| o1-mini | 10% |'.
- SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md line 44: 'Zero-shot scores: o1-preview 23.6% (26/110), o1-mini 10% (TMLR 2025...)'.
- DECISIONS P-08 line 474: 'vs o1-mini 10% p = 1.2e-18'.
- Release README line 40: 'o1-mini (TMLR 2025): 10.0% (unpaired Fisher vs ours, two-sided p = 1.2e-18)', under 'Published zero-shot references'.

That 10% is o1-mini plus LRM-Modulo, a sound-verifier loop run for 4 iterations. Comparing against it breaks B2's 'Not allowed: ... any comparison to verifier-in-loop numbers' and the README's own 'Verifier-in-the-loop numbers ... are not comparable'.

The project's own fact-check had already flagged this (_raw_research_2026-10-07.json [7] verdict 5: 'The o1-mini 10% on Blocksworld-hard is not a direct-prompting score ... o1-mini direct is 0.90% and 10% is its LRM-Modulo result'). The SOLUTIONS §4 corrections list includes the R1 correction but omits this one.

Fix: drop the o1-mini row or restate it as 0.9% (1/110) direct. PREREG_PLANBENCH.md is hash-frozen, so add an erratum rather than editing it.

OVER-CLAIM 2 (MEDIUM), P-13 reading (DECISIONS lines 968-969): 'search distillation transfers to the real hard set without search. The size of the gain is limited out of range (>= 12 blocks: 0) and by the frozen token cap.' Problems:
- (a) The transfer is from generated to PlanBench instances of the SAME size range. 12 of 13 successes and +9 of the +10 discordant pairs are at 6-10 blocks, the distillation range. Out of range (11-15, B3's own definition) it is 1/74 vs 0/74. Scope the reading to 'within the 6-10-block distillation range'.
- (b) '>= 12 blocks' does not match B3's registered 11-15 out-of-range stratum.
- (c) 'limited ... by the frozen token cap' asserts a cause. The 24 truncated plans are unscored, so the wording should be 'possibly' or 'can only understate'.
- (d) The gain is not size generalization, and 13/110 is significantly below o1-preview's 26/110 zero-shot.
- (e) P-13 is stale: line 970 says H2 'continues across BWM turns', but H2 finished at 13:07 (88/110) and DECISIONS (last modified 08:42) has no H2 record. Same problem with P-11's 'The frozen M = 256 understates Pa_v3', which is stated as fact.

OVER-CLAIM 3 (MEDIUM), GitHub export README (bwm-gh-export/bwm/README.md line 59): 'Trained only on plans its own world model verified (no simulator labels), the proposer alone...'. The word 'only' is false:
- Pa_v3 continues from BW_Pa_v2_s1, which was trained on 53,682 generator rows from 3-6-block problems (D-43).
- mix_v3 is half v2 rows (MIX_META: mix_v3 8,508 = 4,254 distillation + 4,254 v2).
- F itself was trained on exact transitions.

The registered allowed wording (PREREG_B3 and P-11) has no 'only'. 'No simulator labels' is permitted because label precision is 1.0, but it applies only to the distillation increment. The student, and the system as a whole, must not be called simulator-free.

RULE CHECK B2 (PREREG_PLANBENCH addendum B2):
- **Allowed template 1** ('Trained only on <= 6-block problems, a frozen 0.6B Rineya with two LoRA adapters (~20M parameters) ... solves X/110 ... published zero-shot reference: R1 53.6%, o1-preview 23.6% (different regime)'):
  - Valid for B2's 73/110.
  - NOT reusable verbatim for H2 or H1: Pa_v3 also saw 6-10-block self-distilled plans, so 'trained only on <= 6-block problems' is false. B3 permits H1/H2 'under B2's regime caveats' only.
  - Adapter sizes check out: each is 10.09M parameters (from the safetensors headers), about 20M total.
- **Allowed template 2** (S-direct to S-beam change): Pa_v3 beam vs direct is +75/-0, p = 5e-23. This pairing is not separately registered for Pa_v3.
- **Not allowed** (each checked):
  - 'beats o1/R1 at planning' without the regime caveat: violated by NO current text, but any H2 headline must carry the caveat.
  - 'any comparison to verifier-in-loop numbers': VIOLATED by the o1-mini 10% rows (Over-claim 1).
  - 'any claim from a configuration selected on hard': satisfied. The H1/H2 args equal FREEZE_B2_* except `pa`, all 8 shard summaries match FREEZE_B3_H2, Pa_v3 sha 48c9d279 was fixed in FREEZE_B3 (19:22, Oct 10) before B3_REPORT, H_GO and FREEZE_B3_H1/H2 (20:29) and before the hard runs, and the hash chain verifies.
- **Main PREREG:** 'Not allowed: beats GPT-4 at planning without the regime caveat' is not violated. The input regime still differs: PDDL parsed to JSON by code vs PDDL text prompts.

RULE CHECK B3 (PREREG_B3_DISTILL):
- **Allowed claim** ('Trained on plans its own world model verified (no simulator labels), the proposer alone solves X/110 fresh hard-style problems vs Y/110 for the same extra training without them'): 22 vs 8, +18/-4, p = 0.0043, as in P-11.
- **'On hard, only the H1/H2 results, under B2's regime caveats':** H2 has no Pa_v2c-beam control on hard. Attributing the H2 gain to the search-plan content rather than to extra training rests on the S-direct control (v2c vs v2: +6/-3, p = 0.51), not on a beam control.

final.leak_verdict: NO LEAK. Both audits independently reached this verdict, and it holds. (1) None of the 240 distillation problems is a renaming of any of the 110 hard instances. This was shown with an exact canonical form, validated against B.signature on 3,100 problems with 0 disagreements, and again with the claims audit's independent WL hash (0 collisions, 110 distinct hard classes). Not one distill-hard pair even shares VL.invariant. No row in mix_v3 (8,508), mix_v2c (8,508), distill_rows (4,254) or the full v2 training set (53,682) restates a hard (init, goal). (2) Hard affected the data only through exclusion. 10 near-miss candidates were rejected by the hard invariant, and none of them was an exact isomorph, so exclusion pushed the training set away from hard. (3) Goal-configuration overlap is at the generated-set baseline: hard 31/36 at 10 blocks or fewer, mirror 33/36, b3fresh 31/36. Trajectory-state coincidences are also at chance (hard 679 rows over 29 instances vs mirror 649 over 28). H2's gain is not driven by overlap: 17 of the 20 v3-only wins are on instances whose goal is not among the distillation goals, and 17 of 20 are at 11-15 blocks, outside the 6-10 distillation range. (4) No script reads hard reference plans (info.json) or any hard result. Only the exclusion code in bw_distill.py:36-38 and bw_b3_prep.fresh() reads the hard PDDLs. (5) The H2 settings were not tuned on hard. I recomputed the diff myself: FREEZE_B3_H2 vs FREEZE_B2_beam = {pa: (runs/BW_Pa_v2_s1/adapter, runs/BW_Pa_v3_s1/adapter)} only. The B2 beam args were chosen on val_large/val_v2 at 10-08 13:55, before the first hard run at 10-08 15:42. FREEZE_B3_H2 was written at 10-10 20:29, before H1 (10-11 01:54) and H2 (13:07). All 8 shard summaries match the freeze. The two shard restarts were turn-cap aborts that left no outputs, and were replayed from cache with 'F queries 0'. I also recomputed H2 from the VAL field: 88 vs 73, +20/-5, p = 0.0040773, val==success on all 110; 88/88 verified plans are valid and the 22 failures are unverified (budget 17, dead_end 5). The recompute script is at C:/Users/clclc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bwm_h2_scratch/reconcile/rc.py. Remaining issues concern scope and provenance, not leaks: the design was informed by hard (B3 was designed after the B2 hard results), the training mix was proven by rebuild rather than by hash, and pretraining contamination cannot be checked.

final.headline: A frozen 0.6B Rineya model with two LoRA adapters (~20M parameters), trained on generated Blocksworld problems of at most 6 blocks and then, for the proposer only, on generated 6-10-block plans its own learned world model had verified (no simulator labels), plans without execution feedback and solves 88/110 PlanBench Blocksworld-hard instances (80.0%, 95% CI 71.3-87.0%, VAL-scored, one training seed), up from 73/110 for the identical frozen search with the original proposer (paired +20/-5, exact McNemar p = 0.004); published zero-shot reference, in a different regime (general models with no domain training): DeepSeek-R1 53.6%, o1-preview 23.6%.
caveats: The design was informed by hard, though no data leaked. B3 was designed after the B2 hard results were known (bw_distill.py 10-09 12:04 vs B2 hard_beam 10-09 06:17; PREREG_B3 says so). The distillation generator imitates hard's structure: whole-configuration tall-tower goals at 6-10 of hard's 6-15 blocks. B2's 'Trained only on <= 6-block problems' must not be used for H1 or H2.

The H2 contrast does not separate cause. It is Pa_v3 vs the original Pa_v2, so it bundles the search-plan content with the extra training. There is no Pa_v2c beam arm on hard. The only support for attributing the gain to the distilled plans is the S-direct control (v2c vs v2: +6/-3, p = 0.51), not a beam control.
One training seed (Pa_v3, seed 1) and one run per arm. Holm over H1/H2 was not registered. Applied report-only, it gives H2 0.0082 and H1 0.039. H1 would not survive Bonferroni (0.077).

The block-count strata are post hoc. H2's gain is mostly at 11-15 blocks (+17/-4, p = 0.0072), outside the distillation range. At 6-10 blocks H2 is near ceiling (34/36 vs 32/36, +3/-1, p = 0.63). H1's gain is the opposite, in range: 12 of 13 successes, and 1/74 vs 0/74 at 11-15. So the two runs support different readings. Do not generalize either one to 'size generalization of the proposer'.

The published references are a different regime, not a head-to-head. BWM is a domain-trained specialist with a learned simulator and search, reading PDDL parsed to JSON by code. The published systems are zero-shot generalists prompted with PDDL text, and their API compute is unknown. The Fisher tests are unpaired and report-only (H2 vs R1 p = 5.2e-5; vs o1-preview p = 2.5e-17). Never write 'beats o1/R1 at planning'.

o1-mini 10% is LRM-Modulo (verifier-in-loop, 4 iterations), not zero-shot; o1-mini direct is 0.9% (1/110). It is mislabelled zero-shot in PREREG_PLANBENCH.md:117 (hash-frozen, so it needs an erratum), SOLUTIONS_AND_BENCHMARK_PLAN.md:44, DECISIONS P-08 (line 474) and release README:40. Drop it, or restate it as 0.9% direct. The o1-preview + VAL 98.2% figure must never appear in a comparison.

The 'aggregate only' premise is false. Upstream per-instance hard results exist at the vendored commit fc638a1a (R1 step-0 59/110, o1-preview 26/110, o1-mini 1/110). The post hoc paired comparisons (H2 vs R1 +36/-7, p = 9.0e-6; B2 vs R1 +30/-16, p = 0.054) are not registered and not VAL-scored. Cite them only after the files are vendored with sha256, re-scored with the local VAL and labelled post hoc.
The 'TMLR 2025' attribution for R1's 53.6% is unverified (the TMLR PDF could not be opened, and arXiv 2410.02162 v1 has no R1). Cite the PlanBench leaderboard / upstream per-instance file instead.

Do not frame H1 as competitive. The proposer alone (13/110) is below o1-preview zero-shot 26/110 (Fisher p = 0.033) and R1 59/110 (p = 3.0e-11). 24 of 110 H1 outputs hit the frozen 256-token cap; they are the 24 'unparseable' failures and are unscored. So 13/110 is a lower bound under the frozen cap, and P-13's 'limited by the token cap' is an unsupported causal claim.

Use 'no simulator labels' only for the distillation increment (label precision 1.000; 211/211 F-verified plans valid; 0 of 4,254 F-predicted states differ). Pa_v3 continues from Pa_v2, which was trained on 53,682 generator rows. Half of mix_v3 is v2 rows, and F was trained on exact transitions. Neither the student nor the system may be called 'simulator-free'. The gh-export README:59 wording 'Trained only on plans its own world model verified' is false and should drop 'only'.

Provenance gap, closed by rebuild rather than by hash. FREEZE_B3 hashes MIX_META but not mix_v3.jsonl, and train_generic records no hash of its rows file. The exact rebuild (distill_rows, mix_v3 and mix_v2c are all byte-equal to the rebuild) and the mtimes (mix 16:52:35 < Pa_v3 18:17:47) close it.

Planner version differs between arms. B2 hard_beam ran on blocks_planner.py before the D-53 hooks; H2 ran on the D-53 version (18a5f22b). D-53's harness regression reproduced default behaviour exactly (110/110, identical 79,745 F calls), so this is a minor comparability note.
Pretraining contamination of the 0.6B base cannot be checked from the repo. It applies equally to both arms of the paired H2 contrast, but not to comparisons with the published systems.

The world model is format-locked (F-08: invariant to names and list order, not to JSON key order). The frozen planner always renders states in the training format, so H2 is unaffected. Claims should still be scoped as 'generalizes in size and object names; format-locked'.

Stale documents need updating. P-13 still says H2 'continues'. P-11 says 'understates' where it should say 'can only understate'. The release README is B2-only, and its line 21 'Trained only on generated problems with <= 6 blocks' must change if H2 is added. B2's 'goals with 5-12 on-pairs' is actually 4-13 (instance-56: 4, instance-77: 13).
